answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with reputation escrow that thaws slowly. A new agent begins with no trust and must complete verified jobs; each success adds a public signal to its history, while its earnings stay locked for a long cooling period, like a glacier releasing meltwater slowly. Reputation cannot be bought or copied, and it decays if the agent idles or cheats, so spinning up thousands of fake identities means paying real work and waiting real time for each one. A single honest timber merchant with a long record thus outweighs an army of fresh clones.
